title: Yoke reads UTF-8 input and captures UTF-8 output on Windows
when: A shell or harness pipes text into Yoke or captures command output on native Windows, where redirected Python streams otherwise use the ANSI code page.
need: Yoke reads stdin as UTF-8 on every OS, including hook payloads, and removes a leading byte-order mark. Shared CLI text file flags accept the same encoding. Invalid stdin stops the command with stdin_invalid_utf8 and a recovery step. An undecodable hook payload exits with a diagnostic before any hook runs. Native Windows CLI output streams use UTF-8 without changing the console code page. Watched Python children emit UTF-8, and the watcher preserves malformed child bytes as visible escapes in its capture. A reader that closes the pipe early ends output quietly on every OS. Windows reports EINVAL and POSIX reports BrokenPipeError.
surface: yoke CLI entry point and the engines it runs in-process or as children.
review: The Windows suite feeds raw byte pipes into the CLI for messages, feedback, Progress Log and hooks. Native terminal capture exercises cmd.exe, Windows PowerShell and pwsh. For end-to-end Windows proof, send from cmd.exe and PowerShell 7 and read stored replies from each supported harness relay. Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults can replace characters before Yoke receives them.
